title: Rav Chinena the Elder
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: According to Hyman, Ein Yaakov has him speaking in Rav’s name at Berakhot 12b (compare [Berakhot 12b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.12b.2), where the text names Rabbah bar Chinena the Elder). In [Pesachim 75a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.75a.4), Rav Chinena bar Idi asks Rav Ada bar Ahavah: “But did not Rav Chinena the Elder cite Rav Assi in the name of Rabbi Yochanan?” Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim has Rav Chana the Elder in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.
We also find Rav Kahana son of Rav Chinena the Elder in [Pesachim 76b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.76b.10).[^4]

notes.text: The supplied text fully writes Rav Assi, whereas the saved Davidson Pesachim 75a reads Rabbi Assi. Both title forms and the Ein Yaakov/Dikdukei Soferim variants remain distinct.

The consulted Berakhot 12b passages read Rabbah bar Chinena the Elder. The different Ein Yaakov and Dikdukei Soferim readings are Hyman’s edition reports, not independently inspected printed readings.

The consulted [Pesachim 75a:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.75a.4) includes the intermediate speaker Assi and calls him Rabbi Assi. The shorter chain and the Chana spelling are Hyman’s report of Dikdukei Soferim.

The consulted Berakhot repeats the name Rabbah bar Chinena the Elder and the transmission in Rav’s name at [Berakhot 12b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.12b.6) and [Berakhot 12b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.12b.9). The reported Ein Yaakov reading is Hyman’s. The linked Pesachim calls Kahana the son of Rav Chinena the Elder in a teaching about bread baked alongside meat.
